scope: Independent512x64 research macro physical views. This does not replace the existing SoC SRAMs, characterize their timing, or close full-chip LVS.

geometry_controls.scope: Standalone macro abstract geometry and port consistency, plus three actual malformed LEF imports. No routing-access, Liberty, antenna or full-chip physical acceptance.

pin_access.scope: Standalone R0 carrier and one placement only. Supply access, full routing, antenna and Liberty/SoC qualification remain separate.

inputs.scope: Complete input GDS; unmodified upstream antenna deck, deep mode; recommended checks off; no acceptance inherited for other decks or layouts
Complete input GDS; unmodified upstream density deck, deep mode; recommended checks off; no acceptance inherited for other decks or layouts

limitations: Only the R0 orientation and one standalone placement are tested. No fabricated timing model or full-chip integration is claimed.

LEF initially had no clock access; later openings preserve every actual drawing/fill conductor and cut while exposing the empty route to the macro boundary. Both failed access experiments remain in the archive.
The router warns that some LEF58 enclosure rules are unsupported. Its access result is not a foundry DRC verdict.
Supply routing, complete signal routing, native bit-mask/MEN/BIST interface compatibility, transistor PVT and125MHz characterization, Liberty and full-chip acceptance remain open.

Initial normalization incorrectly compared rendered text boxes as physical polygons; corrected normalization compares physical geometry and text anchors separately. API/deprecation/power-net setup errors are preserved.

Initial LVS auditor used host Python without klayout.db; the identical LVS database was audited successfully with the pinned bundled runtime. Full DRC and extraction/comparison were not waived or replaced.
